key_insight: Bismuth-based double-perovskites show promise as alternative materials for efficient photovoltaics, overcoming limitations of lead-based perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a pathway for the development of lead-free solar cells that maintain performance and stability.
method: Optoelectronic characterization of Bi2FeCrO6 and Bi2MnCrO6 thin films.
Solution-deposited films demonstrate a double-perovskite structure with monoclinic symmetry.
Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy used to determine band-edges.
evidence_signal: The BMCO-based solar cell achieved a maximum conversion efficiency of 3.56%, indicating potential for improvement.
watch_item: Defect control is crucial for enhancing conversion efficiency; uncontrolled defects could hinder performance.
paper_title: Beyond lead halide perovskites: visible light photovoltaics with phase engineered bismuth-based oxide double-perovskites, Bi2MCrO6 (M = Fe, Mn)
